_meta.indication: Toviaz is indicated for the treatment of overactive bladder with symptoms of urge urinary incontinence, urgency, and frequency.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, fixed-dose, parallel-arm study comparing fesoterodine 4 mg/day, fesoterodine 8 mg/day, placebo, and tolterodine 4 mg/day over 12 weeks (conducted in Europe/Australia/New Zealand/South Africa).
pivotal_trials.population: Adults >18 years with a minimum 6-month history of OAB or urge incontinence, at least 3 urge incontinence episodes and at least 8 micturitions per 24 hours during the diary period.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: change in number of micturitions per 24 hours and change in number of urge incontinence episodes per 24 hours from baseline to week 12.
pivotal_trials.n: Total 1135 randomized (Placebo 285, Feso 4 mg 272, Feso 8 mg 288, Tolt 4 mg 290).
pivotal_trials.result: At week 12, reduction in micturitions was -1.90 (4 mg) and -1.99 (8 mg) vs -1.08 placebo (treatment differences -0.82 and -0.91, both p<.05); reduction in urge incontinence episodes was -1.94 (4 mg) and -2.22 (8 mg) vs -1.14 placebo (treatment differences -0.80 and -1.08, both p<.05).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, fixed-dose, parallel-arm study comparing fesoterodine 4 mg/day, fesoterodine 8 mg/day, and placebo over 12 weeks (conducted in the USA).
pivotal_trials.population: Adults >18 years with a minimum 6-month history of OAB or urge incontinence, at least 3 urge incontinence episodes and at least 8 micturitions per 24 hours during the diary period.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: change in number of micturitions per 24 hours and change in number of urge incontinence episodes per 24 hours from baseline to week 12.
pivotal_trials.n: Total 836 randomized (Placebo 274, Feso 4 mg 283, Feso 8 mg 279).
pivotal_trials.result: At week 12, reduction in micturitions was -1.62 (4 mg) and -2.10 (8 mg) vs -1.09 placebo (treatment differences -0.53, p=0.032; and -1.00, p<.05); reduction in urge incontinence episodes was -1.60 (4 mg) and -2.21 (8 mg) vs -0.83 placebo (treatment differences -0.77 and -1.38, both p<.05).

key_safety: Most common adverse event was dry mouth (18.8% at 4 mg, 34.6% at 8 mg vs 7.0% placebo); second most common was constipation (4.2% at 4 mg, 6.0% at 8 mg vs 2.0% placebo). Other antimuscarinic effects included dry eyes, dysuria, and urinary retention. Contraindicated in patients with urinary retention, gastric retention, or uncontrolled narrow-angle glaucoma.
target_moa: Fesoterodine is a competitive muscarinic receptor antagonist; it is rapidly hydrolyzed to its active metabolite 5-hydroxymethyl tolterodine, which inhibits muscarinic receptors in the bladder (involved in urinary bladder smooth muscle contraction).

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an advisory committee because the product is a member of the class of antimuscarinic products for overactive bladder and posed no unique concerns.

description.text: Added treatment of neurogenic detrusor overactivity (NDO) in pediatric patients 6 years and older weighing greater than 25 kg

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the treatment of neurogenic detrusor overactivity (NDO) in pediatric patients 6 years of age and older and weighing greater than 25 kg.

summary.text: Toviaz was approved through the standard NDA pathway for treatment of overactive bladder; it was not referred to an advisory committee as a member of the established antimuscarinic drug class. The application was originally submitted March 17, 2006 and received an "approvable" action January 25, 2007 (based primarily on the manufacturing facility not being available for inspection); a complete response was submitted May 1, 2008 and the drug was approved October 31, 2008 with a deferred PREA pediatric study.
